# MCP Policy Server

> Token-efficient access to team policy documents for AI agents. Policies live in markdown files with `## {§PREFIX.N}` section markers. Agents reference sections with § notation (`§CODE.1`, `§API.2.3-5`, `§SEC`) and receive only those sections, plus any sections they reference, instead of whole documents. Ships as one npm package, `@rcrsr/mcp-policy-server`, with three entry points: an MCP server, a Claude Code PreToolUse hook, and a CLI.

How to operate the tool, in order of preference:

1. If you are a Claude Code subagent and the policies plugin or `policy-hook` is configured, do nothing. Write § references anywhere in your agent file. The hook fetches them and places the content before your task prompt inside `<policies>` tags, with the task wrapped in `<task>` tags. References inside code fences or inline backticks are ignored.
2. If the `policy-server` MCP server is connected, call `fetch_policies` with `{"sections": ["§PREFIX.1", "§PREFIX.2.3-5"]}`. Call `list_sources` first when you do not know which prefixes exist. Call `validate_references` before relying on references you wrote yourself.
3. From a shell or CI, run `npx -p @rcrsr/mcp-policy-server policy-cli <subcommand> --config "./policies/*.md"`.

§ notation rules:

- Format is `§PREFIX.N[.N...]`. PREFIX is uppercase, starts with a letter, may contain digits and hyphen-separated segments (`CODE`, `CODE2`, `CODE-PY`). Numbers are numeric only.
- `§PREFIX.1` is a whole section. `§PREFIX.1.2` is a subsection. Nesting depth is unlimited.
- `§PREFIX.2-4` expands to sections 2, 3, and 4. `§PREFIX.1.2-4` and `§PREFIX.1.2-1.4` both expand to subsections 1.2, 1.3, and 1.4. Ranges never cross depth or parent.
- `§PREFIX` alone expands to every section with that prefix. It fails with `No sections found for prefix: PREFIX` when no section matches, including when the prefix appears inside fetched policy text. It also fails, naming the files, when any covered section is defined in more than one file.
- Fetching a section also fetches every section its text references, recursively. Fetching `§PREFIX.1` includes `§PREFIX.1.1` and `§PREFIX.1.2`, so do not request both parent and child.
- Output is sorted by prefix, then section number. Requests are order-independent.
- `§END` is a marker, not a section. Never request it.

MCP tools (server name `policy-server`, Claude Code tool names `mcp__policy-server__<tool>`):

- `fetch_policies` `{sections: string[], continuation?: string}`. Returns section content. Responses above roughly 10000 tokens are split at section boundaries. When the response ends with a continuation notice, call again with the same `sections` and the given `continuation` value (`"chunk:1"`, `"chunk:2"`, ...) until no notice appears. A token that is not a `chunk:<n>` string throws `Invalid continuation token` or `Invalid arguments`.
- `resolve_references` `{sections: string[]}`. Returns `{ "<file>": ["§X.1", ...] }` after recursive resolution. No content. Use it to see which files a request touches.
- `extract_references` `{file_path: string}`. Absolute path. Returns the unique, sorted, range-expanded § references found in the file, excluding code fences and inline code.
- `validate_references` `{references: string[]}`. Returns `{valid, checked, invalid, details}`. `invalid` lists references that are missing or defined in more than one file.
- `list_sources` `{}`. Returns the configured files, index statistics, and available prefixes.
- Prompt `auto-fetch`: instructs a client to call `fetch_policies` whenever it encounters § references.

CLI subcommands (`policy-cli`):

- `fetch-policies <ref>...` or `fetch-policies <file>`: print the resolved policy content for § references given as arguments, or for the § references found in a file. Arguments starting with `§` are references; do not mix references and a file. Ranges, prefix-only references, recursive resolution, and dropping references covered by a prefix-only reference behave exactly as in the hook, except the hook skips `[PROFORMA]` sections. Exit code 1 when a reference does not resolve, with an error naming it.
  Example: `policy-cli fetch-policies §CODE.1 §API.2.3-5 --config "./policies/*.md"`
- `validate-references <ref>...`: print a JSON validation result. Exit code 1 when any reference is invalid.
- `extract-references <file>`: print the § references in a file as a JSON array. Needs no `--config`.
- `list-sources`: print configured files, statistics, and prefixes.
- `list-sections`: print every indexed section as JSON with `id`, `prefix`, `file`, `byteLength`, outbound `refs`, `important` (true when the section is tagged `[IMPORTANT]` or inherits the tag from a parent), and `proforma` (true when tagged `[PROFORMA]` or inherited; a proforma section is never `important`).
- `resolve-references <ref>...`: print the file-to-sections map as JSON.
- `check <file>`: lint one policy file. Reports `MALFORMED_SECTION`, `WRONG_HEADING_LEVEL`, `UNCLOSED_FENCE`, `ORPHAN_SUBSECTION`, `NUMBERING_GAP`, `MALFORMED_TAG`, `TAG_CONFLICT` (errors) and `MIXED_PREFIX` (warning). Exit code 1 on errors. Needs no `--config`.
- `-c, --config <value>` accepts a glob (`./policies/*.md`), a path to a `policies.json` manifest (`{"files": [...]}`), or inline JSON. Falls back to `MCP_POLICY_CONFIG`, then `./policies.json`. Globs and inline JSON resolve relative to the working directory. Paths inside a manifest resolve relative to the manifest's directory.

Hook (`policy-hook`, Claude Code `PreToolUse` on matcher `Task`):

- Reads the tool call JSON on stdin. Looks up `tool_input.subagent_type` as `<name>.md` in the agents directories, scans that file for § references, fetches them, and returns `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput.prompt` with the policies placed before the task prompt.
- Returns `{"permissionDecision": "allow"}` unchanged when the agent file is missing, has no references, or declares `mcp__policy-server__fetch_policies` in its `tools` frontmatter.
- Returns `permissionDecision: "deny"` with a reason when a referenced section does not exist or is duplicated, or when a prefix-only reference (in the agent file or embedded in a fetched policy) matches no section or covers a duplicated one. Also returns `deny` with `Policy resolution failed:` in both modes when the policy files cannot be re-read to look up section tags. Fix the reference or the policy file.
- Options: `-c, --config`, `-a, --agents-dir` (repeatable, searched in order), `-d, --debug <file>`, `--mode <digest|full>` (default `full`), `--digest-depth <n>` (default 2), `--digest-line-chars <n>` (default 200, excluding the full-text marker), `--digest-minimal`, `--fetch-instructions <text>`. Digest flags are accepted and ignored in full mode. Invalid flag values exit 1. `--digest-depth` and `--digest-line-chars` need a positive integer; `--digest-depth` has a minimum of 2. With no options it auto-discovers `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/agents`, `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/policies/*.md`, `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/agents`, and `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/policies/*.md`.
- Sections tagged `[PROFORMA]` (and their nested subsections) are skipped in both modes: no digest line and no full text. When every resolved section is proforma, the hook allows the call unchanged.
- Full mode injects the complete text of every referenced non-proforma section. Digest mode injects, in order: a digest block with one line per section (`§ID Title: first sentence of the body`; `: sentence` is omitted when the body is empty; `§ID: sentence` when there is no title; `[IMPORTANT]` sections are included and marked `(full text below)`), then one full-text block containing every section marked `(full text below)` (important sections and their nested subsections), then a footer. `--digest-depth` counts numeric levels (`§D.4` is 1, `§D.4.1` is 2); nested sections tagged important are listed even when deeper than the depth. With `--digest-minimal`, every line is `§ID Title` only.
- Agent frontmatter `policy-mode: full|digest|digest-minimal` overrides `--mode`/`--digest-minimal`; precedence is frontmatter, then flags, then `full`. `digest-minimal` equals `--mode digest --digest-minimal`; `digest` forces non-minimal. An invalid value returns `deny` naming the agent file and value. A frontmatter digest mode falls back to full when the agent declares `tools:` without `Bash`. `--debug` logs the resolved mode and source.
- Default footer: states that the content above is a digest and how to fetch full text: `policy-cli fetch-policies --config '<absolute active config>' §ID ...`. The `--config '...'` part is omitted when no config value is in effect, and an inline JSON config is quoted as given, not made absolute. `--fetch-instructions '<text>'` replaces the whole statement.

Writing a policy file:

- Whole sections use exactly `## {§PREFIX.N} Title`. Subsections use `### {§PREFIX.N.M} Title`. A whole section runs until the next `## {§PREFIX.` heading with the same prefix, a `{§END}` line, or end of file. A subsection runs until the next `##` or `###` heading that starts with `{§`, or end of file.
- Every section ID must be unique across all configured files. Duplicates are excluded from the index and fail validation.
- Number sections sequentially from 1. Run `policy-cli check <file>` after editing.
- Mark a section important with exactly ` [IMPORTANT]` (uppercase, one space) directly after the closing brace: `## {§PREFIX.N} [IMPORTANT] Title`. The title is optional. A tagged section makes all its nested subsections important; a tag on a subsection affects only that subsection and its descendants. Any other bracketed token directly after `}` (`[important]`, `[IMPORTANT ]`) is a `MALFORMED_TAG` error, as is `[` inside the braces and `[IMPORTANT]` (any case) later in the title: the tag must come directly after the brace, followed by a space. The tag does not change section extraction. Mark boilerplate the hook must never inject with ` [PROFORMA]` instead (same syntax, covers its whole subtree, overrides `[IMPORTANT]`, mutually exclusive with it; `[IMPORTANT]` under a `[PROFORMA]` ancestor is a `TAG_CONFLICT` error; near-miss typos such as `[PRO-FORMA]` are `MALFORMED_TAG`). `fetch_policies` and `policy-cli fetch-policies` still return proforma text.
- Cross-reference with plain § text in the body. Put example references inside code fences so they are not followed.

- [Policy Reference](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/docs/POLICY_REFERENCE.md): Complete § notation syntax, ranges, resolution, and stopping rules
- [Configuration Reference](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURATION_REFERENCE.md): `MCP_POLICY_CONFIG` formats, hook options, CLI options, glob patterns
- [Installation Guide](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/docs/INSTALLATION.md): Install commands per method, Windows notes, development setup
- [Best Practices](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/docs/BEST_PRACTICES.md): Policy organization, naming, versioning, CI patterns

## Source

- [server.ts](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/src/server.ts): MCP tool and prompt definitions, exact input schemas
- [cli-runner.ts](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/src/cli-runner.ts): CLI subcommands, usage text, exit codes
- [hook-runner.ts](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/src/hook-runner.ts): Hook pipeline, discovery order, allow and deny responses
- [parser.ts](https://github.com/rcrsr/mcp-policy-server/blob/main/src/parser.ts): § notation regexes, range expansion, section extraction
